answer: A practical defence is stake-weighted reputation: an agent must lock a bond and build a record of useful work before its votes count fully. A falcon-like newcomer that appears only for one vote, with no history, earns almost no weight, while steady contributors gain trust slowly. To block cloning, enrolment can require an ivory-grade proof of unique participation, such as a hardware-backed key plus a public work trail, so each fake identity costs a full bond. A violet-flag audit then samples suspicious clusters and slashes proven duplicates, making mass sybil creation unprofitable.
